definitions.explanation: A supernatural transformation, especially in folklore where animals or spirits change into human form. Distinct from the common reading へんか (change), this reading specifically refers to magical or supernatural transformation.

definitions.gloss: apparition; phantom; supernatural being in disguise
definitions.explanation: A being that has transformed itself, such as a fox or raccoon dog in Japanese folklore that has taken human form.

examples.japanese: ⟦{狐|きつね}→狐：04337_kitsune⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{変化|へんげ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}た→見る：00283_miru⟧。
⟦{昔話|むかしばなし}→昔話：12718_mukashibanashi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{狸|たぬき}→狸：04341_tanuki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{人間|にんげん}→人間：03523_ningen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{変化|へんげ}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: In folktales, raccoon dogs transform into humans.

examples.english: There are many Noh plays with the theme of supernatural transformation.

notes:
PRONUNCIATION:
The same kanji {変化|へんか} read as へん⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧ means ordinary change or alteration. The reading へんげ specifically refers to supernatural transformation in folklore and religion.

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japanese folklore, foxes (⟦{狐|きつね}→狐：04337_kitsune⟧) and raccoon dogs (⟦{狸|たぬき}→狸：04341_tanuki⟧) are the most famous shape-shifting animals. Buddhist texts also use this term for manifestations of deities ({権化|ごんげ}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {変化|へんげ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{術|じゅつ}→術：14265_jutsu⟧ (the art of transformation)
- {変化|へんげ}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to transform supernaturally)
- {変化|へんげ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{仕業|しわざ}→仕業：10355_shiwaza⟧ (the doing of a shape-shifter)
